description: §15.10.1 (S458 third round, N1) — inside BLOCK-bodied arrows in a component body, prop substitution resolves names like the language does: an object-literal key named like the prop (`{ label: 2 }`, and the realistic `items.map(it => { return { label: …, id: … } })`), regex / string / comment content, a local `let label` / `const label` (then written), and nested parameters (`function g(label)`, `(label) => …`, destructured `({ label }) => …`) are NOT the prop; a shorthand `{ label }` IS a read of it (`{ label: <value> }`). Executed: the joined result proves every value.
rationale: §15.10.1 Shadowing: 'Prop substitution SHALL be shadowing-aware … A `lambda` parameter with the same name is in scope … A local `let`, `const` … with the same name appears earlier in the same lexical scope'; 'Member-access expressions SHALL substitute only the leftmost identifier'. An object key is a property NAME, not an identifier reference.
